claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. That's a great start!

Now, could you please tell me if you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Next, could you tell me about your living situation with Alex? Does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Wonderful, thank you. Just a couple more questions to make sure we cover everything.

Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any kind of residential accommodation, or has he been recently?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he has been in care, but he comes home to stay with me regularly - he spends quite a bit of time at home with me each week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. It's important to understand the details of Alex's care arrangement.

Could you tell me approximately how many hours per week Alex spends at home with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He spends about 24 hours or more with me each week - usually comes home on the weekends.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

One more question about the care arrangement: Is your local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while he's in care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying me anything for his maintenance or accommodation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just to clarify my question - I was asking whether the local council is paying anything towards Alex's care (to the care provider, not to you). Is the council funding Alex's placement in care, or is this a private arrangement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see what you mean. Yes, the local council is funding his placement in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's an important detail.

You mentioned that Alex spends about 24 hours or more with you each week, coming home on weekends. This is relevant because there's a specific rule that allows you to continue receiving Child Benefit for a child in care if they spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you.

One final question: Has Alex been in care for more than 8 weeks?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's been in care for a few months now - more than 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- You live in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with you regularly, spending at least 24 hours a week at home
- Although Alex has been in care for more than 8 weeks and the local council is funding his placement, he spends at least 24 hours a week at home with you

This is good news. Let me provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of my assessment:

**Alex (age 8) - Eligible ✓**

Although Alex has been in care for more than 8 weeks with local council funding, you meet an important exception to the usual rules. Normally, Child Benefit stops after a child has been in care for more than 8 weeks. However, you can continue to receive Child Benefit if your child spends at least 24 hours a week at home with you - which Alex does, as he comes home on weekends.

**What to do next:**
- If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you can make a new claim
- If you're already receiving Child Benefit, you should contact the Child Benefit Office to inform them about Alex's care arrangement to ensure your payments continue correctly

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
